set.body: The pre-release evidence gate reports unlinked-evidence gaps for every closed work item, even though it is documented to check only items in a released milestone. The scope is computed and printed in each message but never used to filter, so 80% of closed items are flagged and the number grows with every item closed. Two of the project's own conventions guarantee false positives: release items are deliberately never given an external ticket, and ops chores close without a plan or a PR. The result is a release gate nobody can act on.
set.title: trace-check --strict ignores its own released-milestone scope

set.body: The project policy file is documented as checked into the codebase, and every agent session depends on it for work-tracking discipline, but it has never been committed. It is not gitignored either locally or globally, so a fresh clone of this repository gets no policy at all and any agent working from that clone runs with none of the rules. The sibling UI repository tracks its equivalent file correctly, which makes this repository the only one missing it. The file is also mode 600 rather than the 644 a repository file should carry.
set.title: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are not tracked in the source repo

set.resolution: Tracked CLAUDE.md and its AGENTS.md symlink; corrected file mode to 644.

set.body: Every plan page opens with the same banner regardless of whether the plan is finished, in progress, or not yet started, even though the record that produces the banner carries that status. Sixteen completed plans and four unstarted ones currently render identically. The related defect that announced plans as status reports was already fixed in v0.19.0; what remains is the missing status distinction and a silent default that hides a schema violation when a status report has no kind.
set.title: Plan banners do not distinguish a completed plan from one in flight

set.resolution: Regenerated current design doc and walkthrough, froze the dated v0.19.1 pair, refreshed user guide and README.
Scoped the gate to the released-milestone set and exempted kind:ops and (for the plan check) unplanned work. 401 gaps -> 16, all genuine.
Banner now names the plan's own state from the leading word of its status prose; unknown prose says nothing rather than guessing. Removed the kind default that hid a schema violation.

set.body: The generated design document and code walkthrough describe implementation details that are no longer true: a merge-ordering tiebreak that was deleted, a version constant three releases stale, and an import the module does not have. Each is the same failure: the regeneration quoted code it did not re-read. Because the wrong text predates the last release, the frozen copy for that release carries it too, and a reader reasoning about merge determinism would be actively misled.
